text:
rachel: Noticed a tail regression on small-seq after the kernel-hint change that prefers aligned pages. Dropping notes.

rachel: baseline small-chat host-parse p95: 210ms
rachel: after-hint p95: 355ms :frowning:

jin: Any flame or perf top?

rachel: perf sample top deltas (canary vs baseline):
```
page_copy_align       2% -> 19%
parse_tokenize        14% -> 27%
grpc_writev           5% -> 10%
kv_lookup             9% -> 8%
```

omar: page_copy_align? We introduced a memalign+page-pad pass to ensure buffers are page-aligned for the new mmapped iovec path. That added an extra memcpy and a conditional memalign on ingress.

jin: Right, the idea was to let the kernel do splice/mmap zero-copy to GPU. But memalign+pad cost kills small requests. Also memalign sometimes falls back to heap which fragments.

perf-bot: CI quick metrics (canary): host-parse CPU +20%, small-chat p95 +68%, alloc-rate +24%, syscall writev count +120%.

rachel: Short-term: revert the page-align hint on canary and roll a sticky small-buffer pool that returns pre-aligned buffers from a fast slab to avoid memalign.

omar: Also check that our KV cache keying uses exact bytes. If we page-pad with zeros we might change hash. We should only align at buffer boundaries, not modify payload. Add kvcache_key_mode=raw/padded tag.

jin: Long-term: make GPU path accept iovec/multi-page descriptors so we don't need to linearize or align for small fragments. That eliminates copies. Design ticket: RTX-6090 kernel-iov-splice.

rachel: Plan: 1) rollback hint (canary) 2) implement slab of pre-aligned 4KB buffers per-worker (no malloc) 3) experiment with iovec-capable kernel in a dev branch. Also prototype a small ingress coalescer to combine tiny frames into a single aligned buffer before kernel path.

omar: For the slab, prefer posix_memalign once at startup for N buffers and then reuse. Track slab_miss_rate metric. If miss -> fallback to malloc and metric fallback_alloc=true.

perf-bot: After revert deployed: host-parse p95 back to 218ms, page_copy_align drop to 3% in perf sample, alloc-rate back to baseline.

jin: Add telemetry: kernel_hint=page_align_on/off, slab_hit=true/false, slab_miss_rate, kvcache_key_mode, ingress_coalesce=true/false. Also include syscall_writev_count panel.

rachel: I'll land revert PR and open slab PR behind feature flag. PRs: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/2780 (revert) and /2781 (slab pool).

omar: Minor note: check NUMA pinning for slab buffers on multi-socket hosts; mis-pinned pages can hurt latency. Add numa_node tag when allocating slabs to confirm locality.

jin: Good catch. Also run a microbench: replay small-chat workload comparing baseline, bad-canary, slab-pool, and iovec-prototype (if available). Collect p50/p95, memcpy time, syscall counts, slab_hit_rate, kvcache hit-rate.

infra-bot: Revert deployed at 14:08 UTC. Monitoring for 15m.

rachel: Post-revert quick numbers (14:25): p95=220ms, slab: will post bench after PR. Filing follow-ups: RTX-6090 (kernel-iov-splice), RTX-6091 (prealigned-slab-pool), RTX-6092 (ingress-coalesce).

omar: Thanks team. Fast detection + rollback. Keep results in the tickets and tag perf dashboards.

rachel: Attaching a small flame screenshot and the microbench replay script to RTX-6091.
